3a29b77ba239361d051c	clang-tidy	bugprone-empty-catch	hmailserver/source/Server/Common/Persistence/SchemaUpgrader.cpp:73	empty catch statements hide issues; to handle exceptions appropriately, consider re-throwing, handling, or avoiding catch altogether	Triaged 26 September 2026 for the 6.3.4 release gate (.gitlab/security-exceptions.yml), the same line in the same file then: This is deliberate: ~NamedUpgradeLock is a destructor and must not throw. MySQLConnection::TryExecute catches internally and reports failure only through its return (MySQLConnection.cpp 429-507), so only std::bad_alloc can reach this catch. A release_lock that fails because the connection broke fails because the session ended, and GET_LOCK dies with the session. The one case left, bad_alloc on a live pooled connection (DatabaseConnectionManager::UpgradeSchema returns it to the pool), would at worst make another walker wait out its 4-hour GET_LOCK and stop with the named error, with no damage to data.

1ef05e3b7b935f5d845f	clang-tidy	bugprone-signed-char-misuse	hmailserver/source/Server/Common/Util/PushSubscriptions.cpp:233	'signed char' to 'unsigned int' conversion; consider casting to 'unsigned char' first. (also cert-str34-c)	Triaged 26 September 2026 for the 6.3.4 release gate (.gitlab/security-exceptions.yml), the same line in the same file then: In PushSubscriptions::Save, endpoint is a String copied from subscription.endpoint (212), so endpoint[i] is a whole wchar_t, which the rule matches as a signed character type. The cast to unsigned int keeps every bit, and a negative 32-bit wchar_t becomes a value above 0x7E and is refused by `unit < 0x21 || unit > 0x7E`. Casting through unsigned char would truncate, U+0141 to 0x41 for example, and let a non-ASCII character reach the push request line.
